history.period: 9th-10th century CE (sources vary; ASI dating also cited as 10th-12th century CE)
history.summary: ARCHAEOLOGICAL RUINS - not a functioning temple, but an ASI-protected site of ancient temple remains, so keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV town 'Sonitpur' is the district, not the town - corrected to Tezpur; the ruins lie on the right bank of the Brahmaputra near the Bhairavi temple, close to Tezpur town. Believed to be a 9th-10th century CE Panchayatana-style complex, attributed to the Pala period, with a presumed central Vishnu shrine and four Shiva shrines at the corners plus an isolated temple on the north-eastern side; Gupta-style artistry is evident, including a cross-shaped bracket lintel with kirtimukha panels and Dashavatara (ten incarnations of Vishnu) carvings. Scholars attribute its destruction to a devastating earthquake; several pillars and wall fragments were moved to Cole Park (Chitralekha Udyan) in Tezpur town. Dating is conflicted across sources: 9th-10th c. (tourism sites), 10th-12th c. (ASI per some sources), Gupta-era/8th-9th c. stylistic claims in visitor reviews.

name: Bamuni Hills Ruins
town_description: Tezpur, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Sonitpur district, is often called the cultural capital of Assam for its traditions of music, drama and the arts. Ancient as Sonitpur - the 'city of blood' of Banasura legend - it mixes mythic sites (Agnigarh, Bamuni Hills) with colonial-era institutions and parks.

travel.railway: Dekargaon Railway Station, about 10 km away
travel.road: On the right bank of the Brahmaputra near the Bhairavi temple, close to Tezpur town; Tezpur connects to Guwahati by road (NH-27)
